query: What are the time and memory complexity (big-O) formulas and typical empirical constants for in_bag construction, per-tree prediction storage, OOB aggregation, and parallel quantile selection as functions of n_samples and n_trees?

response.query: What are the time and memory complexity (big-O) formulas and typical empirical constants for in_bag construction, per-tree prediction storage, OOB aggregation, and parallel quantile selection as functions of n_samples and n_trees?
response.answer: In_bag construction is O(n_samples * n_trees), per-tree prediction storage is O(n_samples * n_trees), OOB aggregation is O(n_samples * n_trees), and parallel quantile selection is O(n_samples * log(n_samples)).

results.title: Understanding Big O Notation, Time Complexity, and Space Complexity
results.content: # Understanding Big O Notation, Time Complexity, and Space Complexity | by Manik Mia | Medium. # **Understanding Big O Notation, Time Complexity, and Space Complexity**. Big O notation is a mathematical notation used in computer science to describe the efficiency of algorithms. It helps developers understand how the performance of an algorithm scales as the size of the input grows. Additionally, analyzing both time and space complexity allows developers to balance execution speed and memory usage. Big O notation provides a way to classify algorithms based on their time or space complexity. It expresses the worst-case or upper-bound performance of an algorithm, giving an estimate of how execution time or space requirements increase with input size. ## Time Complexity. Time complexity measures how the execution time of an algorithm changes with the size of the input. It helps developers predict the performance of an algorithm as the input grows. *   The execution time increases proportionally with input size.
